text:
Looking at the diff: `case 'hrs'` in the hours group was replaced with `case ""`.

Tracing whether `type` can ever be `""`: `type = (match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase()`. The regex group `(milliseconds?|msecs?|...)?` either doesn't participate (yielding `undefined`, which the `|| 'ms'` converts to `'ms'`) or matches one of the non-empty alternatives. It can never capture an empty string — and even if it could, `"" || 'ms'` evaluates to `'ms'`. So `case ""` is dead code.

Meanwhile, the regex still matches `'hrs'` inputs (via the `hrs?` alternative), so `ms('2hrs')` parses successfully with `match[2] = 'hrs'`, but the switch no longer contains a `case 'hrs'`, so it falls through to `default` and returns `undefined` instead of `7200000`. This is documented behavior (the README even shows `ms('2.5 hrs')`), and the existing suite apparently doesn't exercise `'hrs'`, which is why it stays green.

So the change is a real, observable regression.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses \"hrs\" as hours', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2hrs'), 7200000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2.5 hrs'), 9000000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2HRS'), 7200000);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff replaces case 'hrs' with case \"\", which is unreachable because type is (match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase() and can never be an empty string. Since the regex still matches 'hrs' but no switch case handles it anymore, ms('2hrs') now returns undefined instead of 7200000, an observable regression for callers."}
```
